title: ATAC-Seq
scope: The single generic ATAC-Seq library-construction route in the assigned Illumina schematic: native chromatin with accessible DNA is tagmented by adapter-loaded Tn5, yielding fragmented and primed DNA, followed by the combined depicted DNA purification/amplification block and a DNA library. The left assay vignette identifies the target and repeats the substrate; it does not depict a separate chromatin-opening treatment. Tn5 is a catalytic reagent carrying adapter DNA, not a biological material converted into library. No alternative workflow, compartment indexing, pooling, or sequencing/analysis operation is drawn. Fast-ATAC, neuron/freezing and biobank preparations, single-cell implementations, THS-seq, FAIRE-seq and catalogue kit names are contextual mentions rather than schematic targets.

states.label: Open DNA within native chromatin
features: Genomic DNA is shown wrapped around grey nucleosomes with exposed stretches between and beside them; “Open DNA” is a substrate description, not purified naked genomic DNA.

The highlighted left vignette and repeated unhighlighted substrate represent the same accessibility concept. No cell or nucleus boundary is drawn; unfixed nuclei are the paper-supported preparation context.

evidence.locator: Left assay-identification vignette and repeated substrate labelled “Open DNA”: grey nucleosomes joined by exposed DNA; yellow emphasis only in left vignette.

evidence.quote: Because transposons have been shown to integrate into active regulatory elements in vivo12, we hypothesized that transposition by purified Tn5, a prokaryotic transposase, on small numbers of unfixed eukaryotic nuclei would interrogate regions of accessible chromatin.

states.label: Fragmented and primed chromatin DNA
features: Genomic DNA is now discontinuous, with short pink and yellow-green terminal marks and a free central fragment; nucleosome-associated pieces are also still depicted.

The terminal marks are interpreted as transferred sequencing-adapter sequences from the loaded Tn5 complex, supported by the paper and card. The image supplies no color legend, terminal polarity, chemical end groups or barcode identity.

Accessible-site insertion positions and retained genomic inserts physically encode the chromatin-accessibility sampling. The cartoon does not define separate experimental branches for each fragment or nucleosome icon.

states.label: Purified, amplified DNA library
features: Rightmost product is labelled “DNA”: three linear blue DNA-fragment strokes with short pink and yellow-green terminal segments; nucleosomes and transposome icons are absent. The three strokes represent library fragments, not three separate workflow branches.
Genomic DNA fragments, rather than RNA, histones or transposase protein, are the sequencing readout carrier; adapter sequences provide the amplification/sequencing interface.
The library is enriched for accessible-site-derived fragments, not a complete or perfectly specific inventory of all nucleosome-free bases.

operations.label: Insert in regions of open chromatin → Fragmented and primed
operations.description: Adapter-loaded Tn5 transposomes contact exposed genomic DNA in the native chromatin substrate. Tagmentation cuts DNA and transfers adapter sequences, changing continuous chromatin DNA into tagged fragments. The transposome-engaged illustration and the following fragmented/primed illustration are local views of this one coupled transformation, not independent cleavage and adapter-ligation workflows. Grey nucleosomes illustrate relative protection and remain visible on some output pieces.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 transposase is supplied preloaded with sequencing adapters (blue complex with colored strokes in this diagram). It simultaneously fragments and tags DNA; accessible DNA is preferentially attacked because less accessible chromatin reduces transposition. The icon is a reagent/catalyst annotation, not a consumed sample state. “Primed” denotes adapter-tagged fragments available for subsequent PCR; no separate primer-annealing operation is depicted.
operations.information_effect: Insertion sites and genomic sequences between insertions carry information about chromatin accessibility. Enrichment is preferential: lack of a fragment does not prove absolute inaccessibility. The card cautions that mechanical processing can expose previously bound regions, so tagging reports accessibility under the preparation and reaction context rather than perfect in vivo specificity.

operations.label: DNA purification / Amplification
operations.description: The fragmented and adapter-tagged DNA enters the single broad block labelled DNA purification and Amplification. DNA is recovered from the reaction and amplifiable tagged fragments are copied by PCR, producing the depicted free DNA library. The combined block is retained at its drawn granularity; its routine internal handling is not reconstructed.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper identifies the amplification as PCR following purification. PCR uses the adapter-associated priming interface; compatible fragment ends and spacing constrain which tagged molecules become represented.
operations.information_effect: Genomic inserts and insertion-derived ends remain the physical carriers of accessibility information after amplification. Sequencing and genomic mapping can localize accessible sites; paired-end fragment lengths can additionally inform nucleosome packing, as reported by the paper. Those readout operations are explanatory context beyond the diagram endpoint. Recovery and PCR do not guarantee equal or complete representation of tagged molecules.
